assumptions: The remedy the session siren names is `node <clone>/scripts/install-siren.mjs --install-hooks`, a new hooks-only mode, not the issue's suggested `--install`. `--install` refuses off macOS, needs an interactive login shell and `canary` on PATH, and bootstraps the real LaunchAgent label into the user's launchd domain, so it cannot be run verbatim in a test (CI is ubuntu) without touching the real machine. The hooks-only mode copies the clone's hooks/ into $HOME/.claude/hooks/ via the existing installHooks(), which is exactly what clears this finding.
Only the session siren self-checks; the deep siren is run by launchd from the checkout path baked into the plist, not from the ~/.claude/hooks copy, so the issue scopes item 1 to the session siren.

A differing copy is reported as 'older' (the issue's wording) even though a byte compare cannot tell older from locally edited; either way the remedy restores the tracked copy and installHooks keeps the displaced file as a .bak- sibling.

When the marketplace clone exists but has no hooks/<own name>, or the hook cannot read its own path, the siren adds a 'cannot compare ... unverifiable' finding and runs the remaining checks (cannot-verify is a finding, not a pass). An absent clone stays check 3's finding.

--verify keeps the scheduler's state as the headline when the scheduler itself is unhealthy; when the scheduler is healthy but a hook copy is divergent/unreadable/absent the headline state is `hooks-not-current`. The --json report's top-level ok/state/detail now carry the whole verdict; the scheduler-only verdict moved to `scheduler`.
The fc1112 provenance edit corrects a factual claim in a historical record (symlinks -> copies), as the issue asks.
closingKeywordReason: All three Proposal items (self-divergence check, --verify headline, provenance doc drift) and both Acceptance bullets are delivered in this PR.
